concepts.why: The patient presented with vision loss and severe macular changes with associated edema, and the spectral-domain optical coherence tomography findings showed persistent central macular thickness and changes in macular edema over the course of treatment.
The patient had vision loss and the imaging studies showed changes in macular edema under different treatment conditions, which is consistent with retinal vein occlusion.
The patient is 63 years old and presented with vision loss and severe macular changes, which are consistent with age-related macular degeneration.
The patient had severe macular changes with associated edema, which is consistent with diabetic macular edema, although there is no mention of diabetes in the vignette.
The patient has a history of hypertension and presented with vision loss and severe macular changes, which are consistent with hypertensive retinopathy.
The patient has a history of multiple strokes, which is consistent with the diagnosis of stroke.
The patient has a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and multiple strokes, which are all risk factors for cardiovascular disease.
The patient presented with severe macular changes with associated edema, which is consistent with macular edema.
It explains the persistent central macular thickness of 669.8 μm over 12 visits.
